To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

shear bands of a cold-rolled amorphous metal are characterized by a decrease in mass and density and a concomitant increase in free volume, as determined by a correlative analysis of high-resolution HAADF images and EELS and EDX data.
the density of shear bands is different from that of the matrix and that the density can change within shear bands.

the density of shear bands in a cold- rolled metallic glass is higher than in the surrounding matrix and the density of shear band regions within individual shear bands is higher than in other shear band regions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the density changes of shear bands in a metallic glass.
the development of new analytical methods for the determination of local changes in density of metallic glasses.
the determination of density changes between shear bands and the amorphous matrix in a cold- rolled metallic glass using correlative analytical transmission elec- tron microscopy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the density of the shear bands is higher than in the amorphous matrix.
the density of shear bands is lower than the density of the amorphous matrix and that this is due to an increased free volume.
shear bands are regions of higher free volume and lower mass density.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the observed changes in HAADF intensity are a direct measure for changes in the mass and/or density of a specimen.
the observed changes in density are mainly related to changes in the mass and free volume.
HAADF intensities can be used to determine density changes in shear bands.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the HAADF detector intensity can be used to determine density changes in shear bands with high precision and that the method can be used to quantify the amount of free volume and the associated changes of the mass.
density changes can be measured in the nm-scale by using the HAADF detector signal.
density variations can be measured with high spatial resolution and accuracy using HAADF intensities.
